evidence.text: The database describes oracle-bone and bronze forms as an inverted mouth-like top with a lower horizontal mark, sometimes omitted. It reports that the lower mark bends into the present angular lower shape in small-seal forms. This documents graphic change, while leaving the mark’s referent open: it may represent something held in the mouth or a closed mouth.
evidence.title: 漢字「今」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry describes oracle and bronze forms as 亼 above 一, sometimes without the lower stroke. It presents competing interpretations: mouth plus tongue or other mouth-related mark, a graph associated with groaning or chanting and later borrowed for ‘now,’ and Xu Zhongshu’s interpretation of a wooden clapper bell whose sound called people to order. Its account also cites the Shang oracle-bone phrase 今夕其雨 (roughly, ‘Will it rain tonight?’), Heji 20912, and Western Zhou bronze examples. These attest temporal use early; they do not by themselves prove which proposed pictorial account is correct.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：今

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry treats 亼 as a downward-open mouth-like component in graphs including 今, and distinguishes the character 亼 from a visually similar graph. This is the source’s analysis of the component, not independent proof that the original depicted object or its spoken name is known.

evidence.field: 今部 / 說文解字正文及注
evidence.text: The received Shuowen account glosses 今 as ‘this time’ and analyzes it as 从亼从绁, with 绁 identified as 古文及. Duan Yucai treats the parts as an associative analysis involving 及 ‘reach/arrive.’ This is an important historical explanation in the dictionary tradition, but it is not independent confirmation of the graph’s oracle-bone origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字：今

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 今 / 說文解字及字形說明
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen analysis 从亼、乁 and identifies 乁 as an ancient form of 及. It records senses including now, today, and present/current, with later literary examples. Those examples should not be used to date the semantic development earlier than the Shang oracle-bone attestation.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary explicitly classifies 乁 as a variant form of 及. In conjunction with the Shuowen wording, this supports identifying the component’s ancient-form account with 及; it does not establish that every modern rendering of the component has the same shape.
evidence.title: 異體字字典：乁

evidence.text: The entry records 乁 as 古文及 (‘an ancient form of 及’). This is explicit support for the stated historical relationship; it is not evidence that 及 was the graphic ancestor of 乁.

evidence.text: The 吟 entry quotes the Shuowen analysis 从口，今聲. In that later graph, 口 is the semantic element and 今 is explicitly the phonetic element. This independent phonetic role does not depend on resolving what the older graph 今 originally depicted.

evidence.text: The article discusses Warring States manuscript spellings for the word 吟, including a Guodian occurrence written with 金 as a phonetic spelling. It argues that use of 今 as the phonetic element in 吟 may be comparatively late. That cautions against assuming the present 吟 spelling establishes the original pictorial meaning of 今. The author also reports Zhengzhang-system reconstructions for 今 and 吟; these are distinct reconstructions, not exact identity of pronunciation.

gaps: The character-specific official Unicode Unihan pages for 亼 (U+4EBC), 今 (U+4ECA), and 吟 (U+541F) could not be retrieved. Local kMandarin rows were checked, but the requested per-character upstream click-through verification is unavailable.

The external Baxter–Sagart PDF was inaccessible. Exact Baxter–Sagart readings above are transcribed from the local TSV rows only; the local 亼 row is absent from that reconstruction table. Keep those readings distinct from the inspected Zhengzhang system.

No inspected source independently establishes the name or pronunciation of the object in either the mouth/tongue or wooden-clapper interpretation. The reconstructed pronunciation of the temporal word 今 does not establish the name of the depicted object or a donor word. Therefore a whole-graph phonetic-loan account remains a proposal, not a demonstrated sound-based borrowing.

The source’s text rendering of the Shuowen component appears as 绁 in one transcription, while the Taiwan dictionary and Academia Sinica identify the form as 乁/ancient 及. No glyph image was visually inspected, so the exact printed shape and whether the differing character is encoding/OCR corruption remain unresolved.

The identified early oracle attestation supports the temporal sense, but the inspected page gives no individual absolute date for Heji 20912. The Western Zhou bronze examples likewise have no individual years in the inspected account.

The proposed relationship between 今 and root 其 (‘this’) is reported by Wiktionary as a possibility attributed to Schuessler; the inspected material did not establish the semantic path or chronological evidence.

The graphic interpretation of 今 remains disputed. The evidence supports later phonetic use of 今 in 吟, but does not settle whether groaning/chanting was the original word written by 今, or whether the bell and mouth interpretations are correct.

Character-specific Unicode Unihan records for U+4ECA, U+4EBC, and U+541F returned errors, so the local kMandarin rows could not be independently checked against official per-character pages. Current Mandarin readings are therefore not asserted as externally verified evidence here.

The local Baxter–Sagart table rows for 今 and 吟 are reported in the dossier as *[k]r[ə]m and *m-qʰ(r)[ə]m respectively; the external PDF was inaccessible in the earlier repository research, and this invocation did not independently retrieve it. They are not treated as externally verified readings. Zhengzhang krɯm and ŋɡrɯm are reported separately above.

No inspected source independently establishes the name or pronunciation of an object depicted by the mouth/tongue or wooden-clapper proposals. A reconstruction of the temporal word 今 cannot establish a donor word for an object, so a whole-graph phonetic-loan account remains unproven.

The Shang oracle inscription cited as Heji 20912 has no individual absolute date in the inspected account. Its temporal sense is early-attested, but the source does not establish an earlier ‘groan/chant’ sense. Later use of 今 as 吟’s phonetic element does not establish the graph’s original referent.

The source text displays Shuowen’s component inconsistently as 绁 versus 乁. Other inspected references identify 乁 as 古文及; whether 绁 reflects encoding, transcription, or OCR corruption remains unresolved.

The Wikimedia Commons original-image links were recorded on inspected pages but their download fetch attempts returned cache-miss errors. Captions therefore describe the source’s labeled vector redraws without claiming pixel inspection.
